To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a general approach is proposed to prepare transition metal phosphides nanoarrays supported on MXene nanomaterials, which can act as promising non-noble-metal bifunctional electroatalysts for both hydrogen evolution reaction and oxygen evolution reaction in both acidic and alkaline electrolytes.
we have developed a general approach to prepare transition metal phosphide nanosheets supported on 2D Ti3C2 nanosheets through a facile topotactic transformation.

the strong electronic interactions between TMP nanoarrays and Ti3C2 nanosheets can efficiently accelerate the kinetics of the HER/OER reactions and the resulting CoP/TiC2 MXene exhibits excellent electrocatalytic activities and long term stability toward overall water splitting.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of TMP nanoarrays supported on MXene nanoflakes as bifunctional electro-catalysts for pH universal hydrogen generation and alkaline overall electrochemical water splitting.
the synthesis and characterization of transition metal phosphides (TMPPs) on 2D MXene nanosheet support.
the development of highly efficient and stable bifunctional electrochemical water splitting catalysts for practical applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work provides a general approach to the design of advanced TMP/MXene heterostructures with enhanced catalytic performance for overall water splitting.
the CoP/T3C2 MXenes heterostructure is a promising bifunctional catalyst for overall water splitting in alkaline electrolytes.
this study provides a new approach to synthesize highly conductive TMP nanoarrays on Ti3C 2 MXene nanomembranes through topotactic transformation from layered double hydroxides (LDH).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we successfully developed a general strategy to fabricate TMP nanoarrays on MXenes, which could be extended to other TMPs and MXenes for the design of advanced catalysts.
the strong coupling effect at the interface between TMPs and MXene nanosheet can significantly improve the HER and OER activity of TMPs.
the strong coupling effect between MXene and TMPs can efficiently accelerate the kinetics of the HER/OER and thus improve the overall water splitting activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MXene family can be used as a general substrate to support a variety of active materials for electrochemical applications.
the MXene family could serve as the underlying support for a variety of advanced electrocaterlysts, which is expected to promote the design of novel catalysts with enhanced activity and durability.
MXene can be a promising support for the synthesis of TMPs for efficient and stable bifunctional electrochemical water splitting.
